description: 2D primitive — one filled polygon, or SEVERAL, drawn from a vertex list (metres, local to the anchor). Emits a Space per polygon.
instructions:
A 2D primitive source — a closed polygon Space built from `points` (a JSON array of [x, y] metre pairs, local to the flow anchor). No geometry input; feed its output into the Space pipeline like a Rectangle.

`points` is wireable: connect a Vertices node's (or Space Geometry's) `val-points` into `valin-points` to DRAW that vertex list. A wired list overrides the typed one. The resolved outline is echoed on `val-points`. Wire `valin-color` to tint it. Used by object decompile to represent a `poly` rule (angled / freeform parts).

MULTIPLE POLYGONS: points accepts either a single outline [[x,y],...] or a LIST of outlines [[[x,y],...],...]. Wire Skeleton val-polygons (Regions mode) straight in to draw every region at once. The echo on val-points mirrors the count — one polygon echoes flat so single-outline consumers such as Inset valin-polygon always match; several echo nested.

LAYER: the `Layer` param names the canvas layer this polygon's Space is rendered on (with Flow Live on). Blank falls back to the node's own Live layer; several polygons sharing a name land on ONE layer. A palette-added Polygon auto-names it Polygon1 / Polygon2 / … .

GROUP COLUMN: a flat list whose rows carry a THIRD number splits into one outline per RUN of equal third value. That is how a Math Engine publishes several outlines at once — an Expression can only emit a rectangular matrix, never the nested form — and it lets the outlines differ in length: build them with `Q = vcat(Q, hcat(ring, fill(rows(ring),1,i)))` inside a loop, the same work-list idiom the engine's own loops use, and wire `val-Q` in. A constant third column is a single outline, i.e. unchanged behaviour. See Workflows/Operations/mitered_join_with_math.json.
